Date: 2026-06-17
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 48 min
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Sanjay Patel (CTO, Aurora), Lena Cho (ML Engineer, Aurora), Marco Ruiz (Infra, Aurora)
summary: Redwood Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8). Covered quality-vs-latency tradeoffs, recommended profiles for Aurora's customer-facing summarization and search models, and next steps for a short pilot benchmark. Customer concerned about latency tail, data residency, and security (KMS/SOC2). Agreed to run benchmarks on Aurora sample prompts and deliver a pilot proposal.
topics:
1) INT8 vs FP8 overview and tradeoffs
2) Redwood Optimize profiling & automated recommendations
3) Benchmark methodology: latency percentiles, quality evals, prompt sets
4) Dedicated vs hosted implications for quantization
5) Security/compliance questions (KMS, audit logs, SSO)
6) Next steps and pilot scope
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, with Diego our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Sanjay: Good thanks, we got a lot to cover, mostly around quantization and tail latencies.
[00:22] Diego: Great. Quick agenda — we'll run through INT8 and FP8 profiles, show Optimize recommendations in the Console, and then talk pilot benchmarks. We'll try to keep it practical.
[00:36] Lena: Awesome. Quick context: our main production model is a 13B summarization model, we run it for customer emails and realtime snippets. Latency 95th is our pain.
[00:48] Marco: Also important — we need VPC or private deployment eventually, can't send PII to hosted without encryption at rest w/ customer KMS.
[00:58] Maya: Totally noted. We'll talk security too. Diego, could you start with high level on INT8 vs FP8?
[01:08] Diego: Yeah, so INT8 basically quantizes weights to 8-bit integer which gives large memory and throughput wins. FP8 keeps floating point but lower precision — sometimes quality is higher than INT8 especially on instruction-like tasks. But it depends on model & prompts.
[01:26] Diego: In our Optimize toolkit we profile a model across a set of prompts, run quality evals — rouge/bertscore-ish, and produce a quality vs latency curve. We'll show a couple of example curves.
[01:37] Sanjay: When you say "profile" are you doing prefix caching and batch assumptions? Our workload is small batch low-latency.
[01:44] Diego: Yes we profile with your expected concurrency, sequence lengths, and we model KV cache hit rates, prefix caching too. For low-batch realtime we bias towards lower latency configs.
[01:56] Lena: Do you have observed examples where FP8 actually beats INT8 on quality?
[02:03] Diego: Yeah, for some generation-heavy instruction tasks FP8 maintained better long-form coherence. INT8 sometimes introduces more quantization noise — but with per-channel calibration and the right kernels it's close.
[02:18] Maya: I'll pull up the Console demo — Optimize -> Quantization Profiles.
[02:26] Diego: (screen share) Okay here's an Aurora-like profile we prepped: baseline FP16, INT8 quantized, FP8 quantized. X-axis is 95th latency, Y-axis is relative quality score. You can see FP8 sits at similar quality to FP16 with ~20-30% latency reduction, INT8 is lower latency but quality delta is sometimes -2 to -6% on our metric.
[02:50] Sanjay: Hmm 2-6% quality drop on INT8 is potentially unacceptable for summaries. How do you measure that metric?
[02:58] Diego: It's a composite: ROUGE-L + semantic similarity (we use an embedding cos-sim), and we run a small human eval sample for edge cases. We can tune thresholds per customer.
[03:12] Lena: Could we use cascading? e.g., use INT8 for quick first-pass and fall back to FP8/FP16 for low-confidence outputs?
[03:20] Diego: Yep, Redwood supports routing policies and fallbacks — you can do fast path INT8 and then route low-confidence to FP8 or a higher-tier model. That helps cost control while keeping quality.
[03:34] Marco: What about dedicated vs hosted? If we go Dedicated in our VPC will we still get the same quantized kernels?
[03:41] Diego: Yes, the runtime and kernels are the same; Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and network controls. On Dedicated we can also pin specific kernel implementations and keep a custom quant profile. There are some infra setup steps, but functionally it's consistent.
[03:56] Sanjay: Can you walk through an example run — like how you'd set up the benchmark and what artifacts you return?
[04:03] Diego: Sure. We ask for a representative prompt set (300-1,000 prompts), expected concurrency, and target SLOs. We run N runs across configurations: FP16, FP8, INT8 with several batching configs. We report latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), token throughput, and quality deltas. We provide a CSV and plots in the Console and a spreadsheet.
[04:23] Maya: We'll also include cost estimates — tokens and GPU-time.
[04:27] Sanjay: Good. For our UI product, 95th under 350ms is ideal.
[04:33] Diego: Noted. Our pre-run on a similar 13B model showed INT8 p95 ~280ms, FP8 ~360ms, FP16 ~520ms on the same hardware. But again these numbers vary by sequence length and batch.
[04:49] Lena: Those look good. How confident are you in INT8 stability? We can't have hallucinations increase.
[04:55] Diego: Stability depends on calibration. We run per-layer calibration and evaluate on your dev set. For edge-sensitive tasks we often recommend FP8 or a hybrid approach.
[05:07] Sanjay: Security — can you support our KMS for encryption at rest and bring-your-own-key for Dedicated?
[05:13] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports BYOK KMS integration and audit logs. For Private/Dedicated we can also do HSM integrations. We'll send the SOC2/ISO docs.
[05:24] Marco: Also need SSO/SAML and RBAC for operators.
[05:28] Maya: We support SSO/SAML, role-based access, and token-level auditing in the Console.
[05:35] Diego: Back to quant — one more nuance: INT8 kernels sometimes require specific CUDA/cuDNN toolchain versions. On Dedicated/Private we'll coordinate versions to match your infra.
[05:48] Sanjay: Got it. Could you explain any corner cases where FP8 performs worse?
[05:55] Diego: FP8 can underperform on extremely long context windows where accumulation error compounds. Also, certain ops or custom layers may not be FP8-friendly. We check model topology during onboarding.
[06:08] Lena: If we do a pilot, what's the shortest timeline?
[06:12] Maya: We can stand up a pilot in 2 weeks if we get prompt set and sample data. Full dedicated onboarding takes longer (~4-6 weeks) for infra and compliance.
[06:22] Sanjay: Pricing — do you have rough delta for INT8 vs FP8 vs FP16?
[06:26] Maya: Roughly, INT8 reduces GPU cost per token by 30-45% vs FP16, FP8 around 15-25%. We'll include detailed cost estimates in the proposal.
[06:36] Marco: Do you support quantization-aware finetuning or just post-training quant?
[06:40] Diego: Currently we do post-training quant and calibration in Optimize. For quant-aware training we'd need to collaborate with your model training pipeline — we can support integrations but that's a separate engagement.
[06:52] Sanjay: Any known regressions on safety classifiers post-quant?
[06:56] Diego: Generally we see minimal impact on classification models, but we always validate safety pipelines separately. We recommend keeping safety classifiers in FP16 or dedicated FP8 configs until validated.
[07:10] Lena: Can you show the Console UI for rolling out a quant profile?
[07:15] Diego: (screen) Here: Optimize -> Quant Profiles -> Create profile. You pick model version, target hardware, and we show recommended quantization presets with expected latency/quality delta. You can enable canary rollout to a percentage of traffic.
[07:32] Maya: That canary is helpful; set 5% to start and monitor quality regressions.
[07:37] Lena: How are regressions surfaced?
[07:39] Diego: Console tracks eval suites, and we tie alerts to prompt set regressions. You can configure thresholds and automatic rollback.
[07:47] Sanjay: Ok, let's talk about the benchmark results you mentioned earlier. Do you have the spreadsheet?
[07:52] Diego: I have a trimmed sample we ran against a synthetic Aurora-like set. (shares link) In this run INT8 delivered p95 280ms, FP8 360ms, FP16 520ms. Quality scores: FP16 baseline 100, FP8 98-101 (varies), INT8 94-97 depending on prompt type.
[08:15] Sanjay: The variety is concerning. Can you narrow to our summaries specifically?
[08:20] Diego: That's why we ask for your prompts. For summarization we often see INT8 closer to 96-98, not high single digits drop. But we will validate on your dev set.
[08:32] Marco: On infra — we use internal GPU fleet, if Dedicated isn't an option initially can we run hosted with a VPC peering?
[08:40] Maya: We offer Private and Dedicated. Hosted can be used with strict data controls, but for PII you probably want Dedicated or Private. We can discuss contractual terms.
[08:51] Lena: Any quick wins you recommend while we run the pilot?
[08:55] Diego: Use prefix caching aggressively for repeated system prompts, reduce sequence length where possible, and try hybrid routing — INT8 fast path, FP8 fallback for low-confidence.
[09:07] Sanjay: Are there tooling integrations for our CI to catch regressions post-quant rollout?
[09:12] Diego: Yes, our CI hooks let you run evals automatically on model push and gate rollouts. We can integrate with Jenkins/GitLab.
[09:20] Marco: Latency tail question: do you batch realtime requests at all? We try to avoid latency spikes from batching.
[09:27] Diego: For low-latency we use micro-batching and continuous batching tuned to your SLO. Optimize simulates arrival patterns so recommendations are realistic.
[09:36] Maya: Okay let's recap next steps — we'll send a proposal, Diego will run a targeted benchmark, and Aurora will provide prompts.
[09:44] Sanjay: Sounds good. One more small Q: do you support per-token pricing model and a way to estimate cost under different quant profiles?
[09:52] Maya: Yes, pricing can be per-token and we provide cost calculators in the proposal based on measured throughput.
[10:00] (longer discussion about legal paperwork and NDAs — audio slightly garbled)
[10:25] Lena: Quick note — our legal wants KMS integration and audit logs proof before pilot.
[10:30] Maya: We'll include the SOC2 and KMS docs in the email.
[10:34] Diego: I'll start the benchmark as soon as we get the prompt set and target SLOs.
[10:40] Sanjay: Great. Any comp vendors we should be aware of? We looked at Triton and some managed providers.
[10:46] Maya: We sometimes see customers evaluate NVIDIA Triton for custom infra or Anthropic/OpenAI for hosted full-stack. We'll include a short competitive note.
[10:55] Marco: Timeline recap: send prompts by Friday, pilot bench starts next week, results by 2026-06-24?
[11:02] Diego: That's feasible.
[11:05] Maya: Okay wrapping up — thanks everyone for time. We'll follow up with the proposal and docs.
[11:12] Sanjay: Thank you.
[11:14] (call ends)
notes: Transcript has occasional transcription errors and generic speaker labels; timestamps approximate. References to product names (e.g., 'Triton') may be slightly mis-transcribed. Shared artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet link (shared in chat), SOC2 and KMS docs to be emailed.
